data.name: Ghawth
data.gender_notes: Ghawth is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic terminology, Ghawth refers to someone who provides help and support, especially in spiritual matters. The term is derived from the Arabic word ghawtha, which means 'to help', 'to support', or 'to aid'. Ghawth can also refer to a helper or supporter in the religious sense, such as a guide or a protector. In the Quran, Allah is described as the ultimate Ghawth, the Helper and Supporter of believers.
data.spiritual_meaning: A beacon of guidance and support in times of need.
data.etymology: Ghawth belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghawth total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: غوث
in_arabic.meaning: واحد من أحرار الله، ومرجع المظلومين، ومحقق الحق
in_arabic.long_meaning: غوث هو مصطلح عربي يعني واحد من أحرار الله، ومرجع المظلومين، ومحقق الحق. يُستخدم هذا المصطلح لوصف الشخص الذي يُعتبر مصدر إلهي للسلطة، والقوة، والعدالة. في الثقافة الإسلامية، يُعتبر غوث من الشخصيات الأهم في التراث الإسلامي، حيث يُعتبر مصدر إلهي للسلطة، والقوة، والعدالة. يُعتبر غوث أيضًا بمثابة محقق الحق، حيث يُعتقد أنّه يسعى إلى إقامة العدالة في الأرض.

in_urdu.name: غوث
in_urdu.meaning: واحد من اھرار اللہ، مرجع مظلومین، محقق حق
in_urdu.long_meaning: غوث کا مصدر ہے گھوثنوں کا، اور یہ ایک اصطلاح ہے جس کا مطلب ہے کہ وہ ایک ایسا شخص ہے جو اللہ کا ایک حریہ ہے، اور مظلومین کے مرجع ہے، اور حق کا محقق ہے۔ اس کے لیے کہا جاتا ہے کہ وہ ایک ایسا شخص ہے جو خدا کے حق کے لیے لڑتا ہے، اور مظلومین کی مدد کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: घौथ
in_hindi.meaning: वहिद में अहरार अल्लाह, मरजू मोज़लूमिन, महक़्क हक़्क
in_hindi.long_meaning: घौथ एक अरबी शब्द है जिसका अर्थ है वहिद में अहरार अल्लाह, मरजू मोज़लूमिन, महक़्क हक़्क। यह शब्द एक ऐसे व्यक्ति को दर्शाता है जो अल्लाह का एक हारी है, और मोज़लूम लोगों का मरजू है, और हक़्क का महक़्क है।

in_pashto.name: غوث
in_pashto.meaning: واحد له پړاو له الله، مرجع مظلومين، محقق حق
in_pashto.long_meaning: غوث په پښتو کې يو د الله پړاو وړ لوی شخصيت دي، چې په لومړي سره د الله لوري د حق په لیرې د مظلومين مرجع او د حق محقق دي. دغه شخصيت په افغانستان او د پښتنو کې د اسلامي تاریخ او فرهنگ څرنګوالی ځانګړی دی.

in_english.name: Ghawth
in_english.meaning: One of the free men of Allah, refuge of the oppressed, and seeker of truth
in_english.long_meaning: Ghawth is an Arabic term that means one of the free men of Allah, refuge of the oppressed, and seeker of truth. In Islamic tradition, Ghawth is considered a powerful and significant figure who seeks to establish justice and righteousness on earth. He is believed to be a refuge for the oppressed and a champion of truth and justice.

data.cultural_impact: The concept of Ghawth is deeply rooted in Islamic culture, especially among Sufi and mystical traditions. Sufis, who are known for their emphasis on the spiritual aspects of Islam, often seek the guidance and support of a visible or invisible Ghawth. The belief in the existence and power of a Ghawth has also given rise to various religious practices, such as dhikr (remembrance of Allah) and seeking the blessings of religious figures.
data.spiritual_significance: The concept of Ghawth holds great spiritual significance in Islam. It emphasizes the idea that believers are not alone in their spiritual struggles and that Allah has provided them with helpers and guides to assist them on their journey towards Allah. The belief in a Ghawth also serves as a source of comfort and solace for believers, reminding them that they are never abandoned or forsaken by Allah. It is a reminder that Allah is always with us, even in our darkest moments, and that He will provide us with the necessary support and guidance to overcome our challenges. Additionally, the belief in a Ghawth encourages believers to help and support one another, reflecting the communal and compassionate nature of Islam.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, in his book 'Al-Isabah fi Tamyiz as-Sahabah', mentions a scholar named Al-Ghawth al-Akbar ibn al-Qasim. He was a famous Sufi saint and scholar of the 4th century AH (10th century CE) and was known for his extraordinary ability to intercede with Allah for his followers. He was also renowned for his scholarly works and was the teacher of Imam al-Haramain al-Muqaddasi.

Ibn Khaldun, in his book 'The Muqaddimah', mentions Al-Ghawth al-Akbar as the founder of the Almoravid dynasty in North Africa in the 5th century AH (11th century CE). He was a Berber leader and a Sufi saint who united the tribes of the Sahara under the banner of Islam and established a powerful empire. He was also known for his piety and his military conquests.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Ghawth' in Islamic tradition refers to a protector or helper, a spiritual guide who intercedes between the believer and the Divine. In modern contexts, this concept is gaining prominence in various Islamic and interfaith communities. On Facebook groups and discussion forums, individuals share their experiences and stories about their personal Ghawths or spiritual guides. On Twitter, the hashtag #myghawth is used to share stories of people's spiritual guides and mentors. On YouTube, there are numerous channels dedicated to Sufi music and poetry, providing a platform for individuals to connect with the spiritual dimension of their faith through the teachings of their Ghawths.
